prompt: a watermleon is $2.99lb, and one watermelon steve wants is 6 pounds. How much will it cost.
response:
To calculate the cost of a 6-pound watermelon when the price is $2.99 per pound, you would multiply the price per pound by the number of pounds:

\[ \text{Cost} = \text{Price per pound} \times \text{Number of pounds} \]

So,

\[ \text{Cost} = \$2.99 \times 6 = \$17.94 \]

Therefore, the 6-pound watermelon will cost Steve $17.94.
